detail.body:
## Purpose

Let a decode instance continue a multimodal request from existing decoder KV, without the media and without encoder capacity. Closes #60521.

This revision is the engine contract only, cut down to the scope discussed in the review (@Isotr0py's [`mm-kv-minimal`](https://github.com/Isotr0py/vllm/tree/mm-kv-minimal) and the reduced scope offered on Oct 26):

- **Generate API:** `features.requires_kv` on `MultiModalFeatures`. All items must already be covered by decoder KV; they carry hashes and placeholder positions only, and the validator rejects serialized payloads in `kwargs_data` / `mm_metadata` and empty hashes. The field is omitted from the wire format when false. `engine_input_from_features` turns a Generate request into the engine input (`mm_requires_kv=True`), and `serve_tokens` uses it.
- **Engine input / feature spec:** `MultiModalInput.mm_requires_kv` and `MultiModalFeatureSpec.requires_kv` carry the same flag per request and per item through IPC.
- **Admission (`InputProcessor`):** KV-only inputs are exempt from the encoder-cache capacity check, so a decode worker with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0}'` admits them. They must carry a nonempty hash and no payload per item, stay within the prompt, and end before the final prompt token, which is always recomputed. Prompt logprobs, pooling, M-RoPE and encoder-decoder models are rejected: M-RoPE derives its positions from the media the input does not carry, so it needs a metadata channel first.
- **Scheduler:** `Request.mm_required_kv_tokens` caches the furthest required position. `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` fails the request (`FINISHED_ERROR`) whenever `num_computed_tokens` is below it, instead of running the decoder over placeholder ids. The check re-applies after preemption and after failed KV loads, and `_update_request_as_session` raises the boundary when a streaming session appends a `requires_kv` feature.
- **Receiver cache / renderers:** the receiver cache skips `requires_kv` features (`data=None` is a deliberate absence, not a cache reference), and the renderers refuse to render such inputs again, so `LLM.generate()` cannot silently drop the requirement.

With the prefill-side hashes and placeholder positions, the decode engine computes the same block hashes as prefill, so the local prefix cache and hash-keyed KV consumers see the same blocks on both sides; the alternative of folding image hashes into `cache_salt` rewrites every decode block hash ([data](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60526#issuecomment-6500329741)).

Removed from the previous revision: the Python `prepare_multimodal_kv_handoff` / `restore_multimodal_kv_handoff` / `export_multimodal_kv_handoff` helpers, the `kv_handoff` version/position-state descriptor and the model fingerprint, the `vllm/inputs/mm_features` package (types and serde stay in `token_in_token_out/`), the `is_embed` round-trip on `PlaceholderRangeInfo` (separate PR), and the long docs section. Callers that embed `AsyncLLM` build the input with `mm_input(...)` plus `mm_requires_kv=True`, or through `engine_input_from_features`.

## Test Plan

CPU-only unit tests on the rebased tree (Linux, Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0, editable install with the precompiled extensions of `866bccf083`):

- `tests/multimodal/test_mm_requires_kv.py` (new): block hashes equal prefill's and differ across images; the receiver cache skips only `requires_kv` features; the flag survives engine IPC; admission with a zero encoder budget, and rejection of payloads, empty hashes, out-of-range spans, spans reaching the last token, prompt logprobs, pooling and M-RoPE models; ordinary multimodal inputs still need encoder capacity; `LLM.generate()` preprocessing and the async renderer reject KV-only inputs.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_media_free_*`: fail-closed below the boundary, re-check after preemption, async load lifecycle (success / failure / cancel, with and without `recompute`), sync load failure, local prefix-cache coverage without a connector (block-granularity limit), streaming-session boundary update.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py` and `test_generate_stream.py`: the wire format omits `requires_kv` when false, restores a media-free engine input, rejects payloads and empty hashes; `serve_tokens` passes the flag through without rendering or media.
- `pre-commit`: ruff, ruff-format and the repo's mypy wrapper on the changed files.

## Test Result

The branch is a single commit, `e8ea00b1cf`, on `main` at `39dbf51839`. Results on this tree (Linux, Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0, one RTX 5090, editable install with the precompiled extensions of `866bccf083`):

- `tests/multimodal/test_mm_requires_kv.py`: 18 passed.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: 299 passed, 3 failed (`test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, `test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output`, `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait`); the same three fail identically on a clean `upstream/main` worktree at `39dbf51839` in this environment, so they are unrelated to this change. All `test_media_free_*` tests and the FSM-abort test pass.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/`: 141 passed in the unit files, and the 29 server-backed tests in `test_serving_tokens.py` and `test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py` (a real `vllm serve`, including the render → generate round trip) pass on the GPU.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render` and `tests/renderers`: identical results on this branch and on clean main (24 passed, 38 fixture errors from models unavailable in this environment), so the renderer guard changes nothing there.
- `tests/multimodal/test_cache.py`: 34 passed; `test_sleep_wake_preserves_mm_cache_consistency` fails identically on clean main here.
- pre-commit on the changed files: ruff-check, ruff-format, the repo's mypy wrapper (the remaining mypy errors in `multimodal/inputs.py`, `scheduler.py` and `input_processor.py` are present on clean main with the same toolchain), typos, markdownlint-cli2, SPDX headers, forbidden and lazy imports, `torch.cuda` calls, test tethering: all passed.

GPU evidence from earlier revisions of the same contract (LLaVA-1.5 / InternVL3, NIXL P/D): [latency and throughput](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60526#issuecomment-6427855468) and [decode-side prefix caching](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60526#issuecomment-6500329741). The engine behaviour exercised there (admission exemption, scheduler coverage check, block-hash parity) is unchanged in this revision; the removed pieces were orchestrator-side helpers.

Dynamo is one motivating caller: [HanFa/dynamo#2](https://github.com/HanFa/dynamo/issues/2), [ai-dynamo/dynamo#15343](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/15343). AI assistance was used (Codex and Claude Code) for the implementation, tests and this description; the commit carries DCO sign-off and attribution trailers.

Otherwise `kv_transfer_params["prompt_token_ids"]` must be a non-empty list of non-negative integers, or the request fails with HTTP 400, as it always does on `/v1/chat/completions/batch`.
 
+## Continuing a multimodal request from existing KV
+
+A decode instance can continue a multimodal request without the media and without encoder capacity when the prompt's KV already exists, locally or through a KV connector. The [Generate API](../serving/online_serving/token_in_token_out.md) input carries the prefill-side `token_ids` and a `features` object with the item hashes and placeholder ranges, and `features.requires_kv: true` states that every item must be covered by decoder KV. The same hashes and positions make the decode instance compute the same block hashes as prefill, so prefix caching and hash-keyed KV stores see the same blocks on both sides. `--limit-mm-per-prompt` may be 0 on the decode instance: such inputs are exempt from the encoder-cache capacity check.
+
+The flag is a requirement, not proof that the KV exists. Before scheduling any computation, the engine checks that the computed tokens cover every required span, including after a preemption or a failed KV load, and fails the request (`finish_reason="error"`) rather than recompute an image from placeholder token ids. Items must carry a nonempty hash and no media payload; the prompt must end with at least one token after the last multimodal span, because the final prompt token is always recomputed; prompt logprobs, pooling, M-RoPE models and encoder-decoder models are not supported. Local prefix-cache hits are whole blocks and never include the block holding the final prompt token, so without a connector the spans must end within the first `floor((N - 1) / block_size) * block_size` tokens of an `N`-token prompt.
+
+Python callers submit the same input directly to `AsyncLLM.generate()` or `LLMEngine.add_request()` as a `MultiModalInput` with `mm_kwargs` set to `None` per item and `mm_requires_kv=True`. `LLM.generate()` and the renderers reject such inputs, because rendering them again would drop the requirement and the media identities.
+
 ## Generate API output modes
 
 When the prefill and decode stages use the [Generate API](../serving/online_serving/token_in_token_out.md) (`/inference/v1/generate`), only the decode response reaches the client, so set `output_mode` on the decode request only. A proxy that reuses the client's request body for the prefill request must reset `output_mode` to `tokens` there. A prefill instance started with `--tokens-only` has no tokenizer and rejects `output_mode: "text"` with a 400.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Engine-side contract for multimodal inputs that require existing KV.
+
+A decode instance without media or encoder capacity continues a multimodal
+request purely from decoder KV. Such an input carries hashes and placeholder
+positions but no media and sets ``mm_requires_kv``: admission accepts it with a
+zero encoder budget, its block hashes equal the prefill engine's, the receiver
+cache skips it, and renderers refuse to render it again. The scheduler side
+(fail the request instead of computing when KV coverage is missing) is covered
+in tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.common.offline import OfflineInferenceMixin
+from vllm.exceptions import VLLMValidationError
+from vllm.inputs import MultiModalInput, mm_input
+from vllm.multimodal.cache import (
+    LruKeyReplicatedReceiverCache,
+    MultiModalCacheMissError,
+)
+from vllm.multimodal.inputs import (
+    MultiModalFeatureSpec,
+    MultiModalKwargsItem,
+    MultiModalKwargsItems,
+    PlaceholderRange,
+)
+from vllm.pooling_params import PoolingParams
+from vllm.renderers.base import BaseRenderer
+from vllm.renderers.params import TokenizeParams
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash
+from vllm.v1.engine.input_processor import InputProcessor
+from vllm.v1.request import Request
+from vllm.v1.serial_utils import MsgpackDecoder, MsgpackEncoder
+
+PROMPT_TOKEN_IDS = [1, 99, 99, 99, 2, 99, 99, 3]
+
+
+def rendered_input(image_hash: str = "a") -> MultiModalInput:
+    """A processed prompt as the renderer hands it to the prefill engine."""
+    return mm_input(
+        prompt_token_ids=list(PROMPT_TOKEN_IDS),
+        mm_kwargs={"image": [None, None]},
+        mm_hashes={"image": [image_hash, "second-image"]},
+        mm_placeholders={
+            "image": [
+                PlaceholderRange(offset=1, length=3),
+                PlaceholderRange(offset=5, length=2),
+            ]
+        },
+        cache_salt="tenant-a",
+    )
+
+
+def kv_only_input(image_hash: str = "a") -> MultiModalInput:
+    """The same prompt as a decode instance receives it: no media, KV required."""
+    prompt = rendered_input(image_hash)
+    prompt["mm_requires_kv"] = True
+    return prompt
+
+
+def without_text_suffix(prompt: MultiModalInput) -> MultiModalInput:
+    # Extend the last image span onto the final prompt token.
+    prompt["mm_placeholders"] = {
+        "image": [
+            PlaceholderRange(offset=1, length=3),
+            PlaceholderRange(offset=5, length=3),
+        ]
+    }
+    return prompt
+
+
+def test_block_hashes_match_prefill_and_differ_across_images():
+    init_none_hash(sha256)
+
+    def block_hashes(prompt: MultiModalInput):
+        features = [
+            MultiModalFeatureSpec(
+                data=None,
+                modality="image",
+                identifier=mm_hash,
+                mm_hash=mm_hash,
+                mm_position=position,
+                requires_kv=prompt.get("mm_requires_kv", False),
+            )
+            for mm_hash, position in zip(
+                prompt["mm_hashes"]["image"], prompt["mm_placeholders"]["image"]
+            )
+        ]
+        return Request(
+            request_id="any-request",
+            prompt_token_ids=prompt["prompt_token_ids"],
+            sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1),
+            pooling_params=None,
+            mm_features=features,
+            cache_salt=prompt["cache_salt"],
+            block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(2, sha256),
+        ).block_hashes
+
+    prefill = block_hashes(rendered_input("a"))
+    decode = block_hashes(kv_only_input("a"))
+    other = block_hashes(kv_only_input("b"))
+    # The continuation reproduces prefill's block hashes exactly, so the local
+    # prefix cache and every hash-keyed KV consumer see the same blocks on both
+    # sides, while a different image still changes every hash.
+    assert prefill == decode
+    assert all(a != b for a, b in zip(decode, other))
+
+
+def test_receiver_cache_skips_only_kv_only_features():
+    cache = LruKeyReplicatedReceiverCache(
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            get_multimodal_config=lambda: SimpleNamespace(mm_processor_cache_gb=0.01)
+        )
+    )
+    feature = MultiModalFeatureSpec(
+        None,
+        "image",
+        "image-a",
+        PlaceholderRange(1, 3),
+        mm_hash="image-a",
+        requires_kv=True,
+    )
+    assert cache.get_and_update_features([feature])[0].data is None
+    feature.requires_kv = False
+    with pytest.raises(MultiModalCacheMissError):
+        cache.get_and_update_features([feature])
+
+
+def test_kv_requirement_survives_engine_ipc_serialization():
+    feature = MultiModalFeatureSpec(
+        None,
+        "image",
+        "a",
+        PlaceholderRange(1, 3, torch.tensor([True, False, True])),
+        mm_hash="a",
+        requires_kv=True,
+    )
+    restored = MsgpackDecoder(MultiModalFeatureSpec).decode(
+        MsgpackEncoder().encode(feature)
+    )
+    assert restored.requires_kv is True
+    assert restored.data is None
+    assert restored.identifier == feature.identifier
+    assert torch.equal(restored.mm_position.is_embed, feature.mm_position.is_embed)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def admission_processor(monkeypatch):
+    """A bare InputProcessor for a decode instance with no encoder capacity."""
+    processor = object.__new__(InputProcessor)
+    processor.model_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        max_model_len=64,
+        runner_type="generate",
+        is_encoder_decoder=False,
+        uses_mrope=False,
+    )
+    processor.vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        model_config=processor.model_config,
+        lora_config=None,
+        speculative_config=None,
+        ec_transfer_config=None,
+        kv_transfer_config=None,
+        watermark_config=None,
+        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            data_parallel_size=1, data_parallel_size_local=1, local_engines_only=False
+        ),
+        cache_config=SimpleNamespace(kv_sharing_fast_prefill=False),
+    )
+    processor.lora_config = None
+    processor.renderer = SimpleNamespace(
+        tokenizer=None, get_eos_token_id=lambda: 2, validate_token_ids=Mock()
+    )
+    processor.generation_config_fields = {}
+    processor.skip_prompt_length_check = False
+    processor.supports_mm_inputs = True
+    processor.mm_encoder_cache_size = 0
+    monkeypatch.setattr(processor, "_validate_params", Mock(return_value=False))
+    return processor
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encoder_cache_size", [0, 16])
+def test_kv_only_input_is_admitted_without_encoder_capacity(
+    admission_processor, encoder_cache_size
+):
+    admission_processor.mm_encoder_cache_size = encoder_cache_size
+    request = admission_processor.process_inputs(
+        "decode", kv_only_input(), SamplingParams(max_tokens=1), ("generate",)
+    )
+    assert request.prompt_token_ids == PROMPT_TOKEN_IDS
+    assert request.cache_salt == "tenant-a"
+    assert request.mm_features is not None
+    assert [f.identifier for f in request.mm_features] == ["a", "second-image"]
+    assert all(f.requires_kv and f.data is None for f in request.mm_features)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("invalid", "error"),
+    [
+        ("suffix", "after the last multimodal span"),
+        ("media", "no media payload"),
+        ("hash", "nonempty hash"),
+        ("bounds", "exceeds the prompt length"),
+        ("prompt_logprobs", "cannot be rescored"),
+        ("pooling", "cannot be rescored"),
+        ("mrope", "M-RoPE"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_kv_only_admission_rejects_invalid_contracts(
+    admission_processor, invalid, error
+):
+    prompt = kv_only_input()
+    params: SamplingParams | PoolingParams = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1)
+    if invalid == "suffix":
+        without_text_suffix(prompt)
+    elif invalid == "media":
+        prompt["mm_kwargs"] = MultiModalKwargsItems(
+            {"image": [MultiModalKwargsItem({}), None]}
+        )
+    elif invalid == "hash":
+        prompt["mm_hashes"] = {"image": ["", "second-image"]}
+    elif invalid == "bounds":
+        prompt["mm_placeholders"] = {

🔴 Image prompts that end on the image placeholder pass export and admission, then always fail with FINISHED_ERROR, even when KV is fully available. The bound check here allows `offset + length == len(prompt_token_ids)`. The scheduler always recomputes the last prompt token, so `num_computed_tokens` stays below `mm_required_kv_tokens`. Fix: reject any `requires_kv` span that reaches the final prompt token (`>=` instead of `>`). Apply this both here and in `engine_input_from_features` (vllm/inputs/mm_features/convert.py:201), so export fails up front before any KV transfer.

<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a LLaVA completion prompt whose last token belongs to the image, such as a raw prompt of only "<image>" or one ending with "<image>". The caller exports it with `prepare_multimodal_kv_handoff` and restores it on decode. `_validate_external_kv_input` (input_processor.py:821-830) only rejects `offset + length > len(prompt_token_ids)`, so it admits a span ending at the last token. Request.__init__ (vllm/v1/request.py:190) then sets `mm_required_kv_tokens = num_prompt_tokens`. A fresh request can never reach that many computed tokens: `get_max_cache_hit_length` caps hits at `num_tokens - 1` (request.py:326), and `_update_waiting_for_remote_kv` sets `num_computed_tokens = num_tokens - 1` after a full async load (scheduler.py:3474-3475). `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` (scheduler.py:2028) therefore adds the request to `missing_multimodal_kv_reqs` every time, and it finishes with FINISHED_ERROR after the KV transfer has already been paid for. 🔴 Prefill and decode instances serving identical weights can reject every KV handoff with "KV handoff model configuration does not match decode". The fingerprint hashes deployment-local values, not just model semantics. `model.model` is the local path or hub id, and `hf_config.to_dict()` carries `_name_or_path` and the installed `transformers_version`. <details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Condition: a P/D deployment where prefill and decode load the same checkpoint from different paths, or mix a hub id with a local mirror, or run different transformers patch versions during a rolling upgrade. 🟡 (optional) KV-only continuations that reuse local prefix KV fail with FINISHED_ERROR whenever the last image span ends inside the prompt's final KV block. Prefix-cache hits are capped at num_tokens-1 and rounded down to whole blocks. This check therefore needs `mm_required_kv_tokens` <= floor((L-1)/block_size)*block_size. LLaVA chat prompts usually have a short text suffix after the image, so many requests hit this. Fix: check this bound at admission or export (input_processor knows cache_config.block_size) so callers get a clear early error. Also state the limit in docs/features/disagg_prefill.md, which currently says local prefix KV works.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A caller follows the documented path: prefill on engine A, then submit the restored input to the same engine with no connector. The docs say "It may reuse local prefix KV without a connector". The KV cache manager returns only full-block hits, bounded by `request.get_max_cache_hit_length()` (num_tokens-1). For a 176-token prompt with block_size 16, num_computed_tokens is therefore 160. Thanks for putting this together — the `requires_kv` semantics and the scheduler-side coverage enforcement (incl. preemption/load-failure rechecks) look like the genuinely new and valuable part of this PR.

One design concern before this goes further: the descriptor/API layer looks like a third parallel schema next to the existing metadata-only paths, and I think it should be aligned with what vLLM already has instead:

1. **Descriptor format**: `MultiModalKvHandoff` largely duplicates the `mm_metadata` serialization in `token_in_token_out/mm_features.py` (hashes, placeholder offsets/lengths). The one real gap there is that `PlaceholderRange.is_embed` is not preserved on main today — fixing that in `mm_features.py` would benefit both the EC path and this one, and seems like a prerequisite either way. Could the handoff payload reuse/extend that format (e.g. model fingerprint as a field) rather than introducing a separate struct?

2. **Admission path**: instead of a new Python-only export/restore API, could this ride on the existing Generate-protocol admission for metadata-only items? `_require_ec_for_metadata_only` currently hard-couples metadata-only features to `ec_transfer_params`; generalizing it to also accept a KV-backed fulfillment claim (e.g. `kv_transfer_params` or an explicit flag) would give KV continuation the same door the EC path already uses, with the scheduler coverage check you added here as the actual enforcement.

The lifecycle contract itself (bypassing the receiver cache for intentionally-absent media, and failing the request whenever KV coverage is missing — including after preemption) has no counterpart in the EC path and does need new logic; my suggestion is only that the descriptor and admission layers not fork from the existing protocol.

Setup: two G7.12xlarge nodes, one RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell GPU each; LLaVA-1.5-7B BF16, TP=1, eager execution, NIXL CPU staging over UCX TCP. Each multimodal configuration used 100 distinct inline JPEGs × 3 rounds, with 595 prompt tokens and 128 output tokens, at concurrency 1 and 8. Cold/warm refers to media caches; KV caches were cleared in both cases so measured requests still required remote KV transfer. There were 3,984 formal requests including text-only controls; startup, warmup and diagnostics were excluded. On the PR head, opting into handoff gave: | Media cache | Concurrency | D preparation p50, full → handoff (ms) | E2E TTFT p50, full → handoff (ms) | Requests/s, full → handoff | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | cold | 1 | 8.76 → 0.54 | 613.0 → 601.7 | 0.334 → 0.335 | | cold | 8 | 13.21 → 0.46 | 1547.2 → 1572.7 | 1.617 → 1.635 | | warm | 1 | 5.55 → 0.53 | 594.6 → 589.6 | 0.336 → 0.337 | | warm | 8 | 7.85 → 0.46 | 1570.1 → 1624.5 | 1.646 → 1.636 | Table p50s pool the requests across three rounds; requests/s is the mean of the three round rates. D preparation measures elapsed time after JSON parsing, including media decoding/rendering or descriptor restore, rather than total-node CPU time. D preparation p50 decreased by **90.4–96.5%**, and the proxy-to-D JSON body decreased from approximately **301.2 KB to 4.87 KB** for these inline images. The full-media baseline already skips D-side vision encoding when remote KV covers the image span; handoff avoids the remaining media-input preparation. The smaller end-to-end improvement is consistent with the preparation stage being a small part of TTFT: cold/C1 saves about 8 ms of D preparation against roughly 613 ms of baseline TTFT. Both paths still transfer the same approximately 304 MiB of KV per request through the CPU/TCP setup. We did not isolate transport/staging time, so this does not establish how much a faster transport would change the result. **Default-path comparison:** throughput was broadly comparable between base and head. Cold/C8 measured 3.17% lower mean throughput on head (1.670 → 1.617 requests/s), with per-round changes of −4.95%, −0.11% and −4.28%. Base itself varied from 1.608 to 1.714 requests/s across rounds. With only three rounds, this small difference is inconclusive: it may reflect run-to-run variability and does not establish a PR-induced regression. Other multimodal conditions and the text-only controls differed by less than 1% in mean throughput. These results also do not establish performance equivalence. **Correctness:** all formal requests completed without request errors or preemption, and decode prompt-source counters recorded external KV for all measured multimodal prompt tokens. Serial full/handoff outputs matched exactly in 600/600 pairs. A separate check with 8 concurrent clients and `max_num_seqs=1` matched all 32 pairs of 128-token outputs and verified real KV arrival with no D-side vision-encoder tasks. With default dynamic batching at C8, full/handoff outputs were not always token-identical; repeated base/full runs also showed differences, so I am not claiming bitwise equivalence under arbitrary batching. These measurements cover one synthetic single-image workload. TTFT is measured to the first token returned by D; P's initial token is not streamed to the client. The supplementary fresh-process TTFT control was interrupted and is excluded from these results.
Minimal example: what the KV handoff carries There are two separate pieces: the **input descriptor** carries token IDs, media hashes, placeholder positions and the KV-coverage requirement; **`kv_transfer_params`** tells the configured connector how to retrieve the matching attention KV. The descriptor contains neither the original image nor the KV tensors. Export/restore alone does not transfer KV or prove it is present. The following extracts the engine calls from the benchmark adapter. Run `prefill` on the P worker and pass its returned JSON to `decode` on the D worker. Both engines must already be initialized with matching model/cache settings and a working NIXL connector. These are Python engine calls, not a standalone launcher or stock HTTP route. ```python """Core engine calls, extracted from worker.py; not a standalone launcher. P and D are separately initialized AsyncLLM engines with matching model/cache settings and a working NIXL connector. Run each function on its owning worker. """ import json import uuid from vllm import SamplingParams async def prefill(p_engine, raw_prompt): # raw_prompt contains text + PIL image; rendered contains image inputs. rendered, descriptor = await p_engine.input_processor.prepare_multimodal_kv_handoff( raw_prompt ) params = SamplingParams( temperature=0, seed=42, max_tokens=1, ignore_eos=True, extra_args={"kv_transfer_params": { "do_remote_decode": True, "do_remote_prefill": False, }}, ) result = None async for result in p_engine.generate(rendered, params, uuid.uuid4().hex): pass assert result is not None and result.kv_transfer_params # Only metadata crosses HTTP here. NIXL moves the actual KV separately. # P's generated token is discarded; D continues from the original prompt. return json.dumps({"input": descriptor, "kv_transfer_params": result.kv_transfer_params}) async def decode(d_engine, wire_json): wire = json.loads(wire_json) restored = d_engine.input_processor.restore_multimodal_kv_handoff(wire["input"]) # No image loading/rendering. requires_kv is enforced by the scheduler. params = SamplingParams( temperature=0, seed=42, max_tokens=32, ignore_eos=True, extra_args={"kv_transfer_params": wire["kv_transfer_params"]}, ) result = None async for result in d_engine.generate(restored, params, uuid.uuid4().hex): pass assert result is not None and result.outputs[0].finish_reason != "error" return list(result.outputs[0].token_ids) ```

TCP remains for HTTP/control traffic; this is a same-host CUDA IPC test, not an EFA/RDMA test. The primary matrix used 100 images/configuration × 3 rounds, totaling 3,984 requests including base/full and text-only controls. The following compares **head/full media → head/handoff**, with p50s pooled across rounds: | Media cache | Concurrency | E2E TTFT p50, full → handoff | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | cold | 1 | 112.76 → 104.06 ms | **−7.7%** | | warm | 1 | 106.91 → 101.49 ms | **−5.1%** | | cold | 8 | 214.68 → 218.29 ms | +1.7% | | warm | 8 | 216.49 → 221.60 ms | +2.4% | All six C1 round/cache pairs improved. I also observed NIXL descriptor counts varying substantially with worker history despite identical KV bytes. 1. The KV-collision bug in Dynamo was Dynamo's to fix, and it was fixed in ai-dynamo/dynamo#15371 by loading and processing the image again on decode. This PR is not a fix for that bug. It is about letting decode skip that media work without reopening the same hazard.

> Hmmm, I think passing --language-model-only should also archieve same targets

2. `--language-model-only` plus a pixel-less text prompt (what smg-project/smg#2640 does) gets close, and this PR is meant to run on exactly such workers: validated KV-only inputs are exempt from the encoder-cache capacity check, so a decode worker with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}'` admits them. The differences are in what the engine can guarantee:

   - **Block identity.** SMG keeps same-size images apart by folding the image hashes into `cache_salt`. The salt enters the first block hash and chains through every later block, so decode's block hashes no longer equal prefill's, and the shared text prefix before the image no longer prefix-caches across requests on the decode side. NIXL does not care because it addresses blocks by id, but anything that looks blocks up by hash (shared-storage and offloading-tier connectors, hash-based reuse between instances) cannot match them. With the real `mm_hashes` and placeholder ranges in `features`, decode computes the same block hashes as prefill and prefix caching keeps its normal semantics.
   - **Fail-closed.** A text-only prompt gives the scheduler nothing that stops it from recomputing the image span from placeholder token ids: after a preemption whose blocks are evicted before the request resumes, or a failed load under `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`, the request completes with HTTP 200 and an answer conditioned on garbage. That is the same class of silent wrong answer as the Dynamo incident with a different trigger, and a caller-side check cannot see it because it happens after admission. `requires_kv` makes the scheduler fail the request instead, for the whole request lifetime.
   - **One implementation.** The Generate API already carries metadata-only `features` for the EC path (#54659). Reusing that door means orchestrators do not each re-derive expanded ids, placeholder layout and hash identity, plus the carve-outs SMG needed (M-RoPE, media refs, n>1), and keep them in sync with vLLM's processors.

If the concern is the amount of surface this adds, I am happy to cut it down to the engine contract only: `is_embed` round-tripping in `PlaceholderRangeInfo`, and `features.requires_kv` with the receiver-cache bypass, the admission exemption and the scheduler coverage check.
